findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The back of the hand washing sink is starting to pull away from the wall. There is about a half inch gap between the wall and the back of the sink. See that the sink is recaulked and sealed to prevent debris accumulation. Ensure that the old caulk is pulled and replaced at the handsink.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: There were personal food items stored above items intended for public consumption inside of the reach in cooler. The personal items were stored above several gallons of milk. Discussed with the PIC that all personal items must be seperate from food intended for public consumption. The PIC moved the items to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. Ensure the employees’ personal items are stored below public food items to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The back of the hand washing sink is in need of recaulking. The current caulk is starting to peel from the wall. Discussed with PIC. Ensure to seal gap between the wall and hand-sink to prevent the buildup of unwanted debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed turning off the faucet handles on the hand-sink without a barrier after the hand-washing process. Discussed with PIC the proper hand-washing technique. Ensure staff are using paper towels as a barrier to shut off faucet handles after drying hands to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The two reach-in freezers to the right of the the triple sink were observed to have a significant buildup of ice on the inside. The facility stores chilled cakes inside the cooler before decorating for customers. PIC noted that the two freezers haven’t been cleaned in a few weeks. Ensure that the inside of the freezers are cleaned and maintained frequently in order to prevent ice build-up. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Doors of ice cream display cases were observed with cracks and areas of disrepair along edges of handles. Owner is working on repairs to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surfaces.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC at time of inspection did not have proof of food manager certification. PIC recently took a food manager course but has not yet received their certification. Another employee with a CFM was present at time of inspection to help oversee operations.  
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee went between tasks without washing hands. Sanitizing solution was prepared at the 3 part sink prior to getting a sample for a customer and preparing a beverage. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. Employees were observed washing hands between tasks as needed for reminder of inspection. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris. PIC was unsure as to the last time the can opener was cleaned. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 Bottom left corner of door sweep was loose and pulled away on the back door. PIC was advised of the issue. 
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by solid, self-closing, tight fitting doors.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Rodent droppings were observed in the corner under dry storage shelves at the north wall by the walk-in freezer (left past the freezer door), by the back door around a bait station, and along the east wall by PVC pipe next to storage shelving.
An old roach egg case was also observed along the base of the walk-in freezer adjacent to dry storage shelving used for bottled water. 
PIC was advised as to the areas of concern and noted they would show the owner so they could let the pest control operator know to provide additional service. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Doors of ice cream display cases were observed with cracks and areas of disrepair along edges of handles. Provide repairs so the doors are smooth and easily cleanable around the handles.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.
